hints.content:
We are given that Julia takes $\pink{10}$ minutes to get ready.

The time it takes Kajal to get ready corresponds to the value of $t$ when $d=0$. To find it, all we need is to substitute $\blue d=\blue 0$ into the formula for $t$:

$\begin{align}
t&=15+6\blue d \\\\
&=15+6\cdot\blue 0 \\\\
&=\pink{15}
\end{align}$

This means Kajal takes $\pink{15}$ minutes to get ready.

**Since $\pink{10}<\pink{15}$, Kajal takes more time to get ready.**

We are also given that Julia takes $40$ minutes to make a delivery $5$ kilometers away. Since she takes $10$ minutes to get ready, we can conclude she rides $\blue{5}$ kilometers in $40-10=\pink{30}$ minutes. We can measure her speed by taking the ratio of the corresponding differences in time and distance:

$ \dfrac{\Delta \pink{\text{Time}}}{\Delta \blue{\text{Distance}}}=\dfrac{30}{5}=\green{6}$

This means that Julia rides one kilometer in $\green{6}$ minutes.

The time it takes Kajal to ride one kilometer is represented by the slope of the graph of $t = 15+6d$. Since the formula for $t$ is in *slope-intercept form*, we can determine that the slope is $\green{6}$. This means that Kajal rides one kilometer in $\green{6}$ minutes.

**Since $\green{6}=\green{6}$, they both ride at the same speed.**

Let's sum it up:

- Kajal takes more time to get ready.

- They both ride at the same speed.

question.content:
Julia and Kajal make deliveries on their bicycles. For each delivery, they need some time to get ready, and then they each ride at a constant speed.

Julia takes $40$ minutes to make a delivery $5$ kilometers away. She uses $10$ minutes of the delivery time to get ready.

The following equation gives the time it takes Kajal to make a delivery (in minutes) as a function of the distance of the delivery (in kilometers).

$t = 15+6d$

**Who takes more time to get ready?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

**Who rides faster?**

[[☃ radio 2]]

choices.content: They both take the same time to get ready
They both ride at the same speed
